title: A Modern Software Supply Chain
description: Interactive Mermaid flow of the nine stages of a software supply chain, each marked with a real-world attack-injection incident, plus the defenses (SBOM, signing, reproducible builds, provenance) mapped to each stage.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Given a real-world supply-chain incident, identify which stage of the chain was compromised.
Determine which defenses (SBOM, code signing, reproducible builds, provenance attestations) would have detected or prevented an attack at a given stage.
Explain why a single compromised build stage poisons every downstream consumer.
educational.prerequisites: Familiarity with version control, package dependencies, and CI/CD build pipelines.

pedagogical.modelType: interactive workflow diagram with attack-injection annotations
pedagogical.assessment: Discussion questions in the lesson plan ask students to map named incidents (SolarWinds, event-stream, NotPetya) to a stage and to the defense that would have caught it.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing a valid code signature proves an artifact is safe (it only proves it was signed; signing keys can be stolen).
Thinking dependency risk is limited to code you wrote, rather than the much larger transitive dependency tree.
